note: Canonical page plan. 'path' is relative to docs/. Groups are writing units. Generated sections (library, mib/tables, explorer, references, glossary, about) are listed under 'generated'.

pages.title: How it all fits together
pages.brief: The front door of the wiki. Explain, for an engineer new to ESA mission operations, the whole chain: on-board software produces parameters; PUS (ECSS-E-ST-70-41) packages them as TM/TC application data inside CCSDS Space Packets; packets ride in CCSDS transfer frames (TM, TC, AOS, USLP) protected by channel coding (TM sync & coding; CLTU for TC); ground stations (ESTRACK, IFMS) hand frames/packets to the control centre via SLE services (RAF/RCF/ROCF/FCLTU) and NCTRS/NIS; the SCOS-2000 mission control system decodes everything using the MIB (Mission Information Base, defined by the SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001); archives (PARC/DARC/FARC) feed dissemination (EDDS, formerly GDDS/TDRS) to scientists. Include one large mermaid flowchart of downlink and uplink and a 'where to go next' map linking to every major section of this wiki. Keep each claim cited.

pages.title: The standards landscape
pages.brief: Who publishes what and how the documents relate: CCSDS (Blue = recommended standards, Magenta = recommended practices, Green = informational reports; explain the colour/number conventions such as 133.0-B-2 and the file naming like 133x0b2e2 meaning edition and corrigendum), ECSS (E-ST engineering standards, E-HB handbooks, E-AS adoption notices that adopt CCSDS books with modifications, DIR drafts for review), ISO adoptions of CCSDS books, ESA/ESOC internal document families (EGOS-MCS-S2K-..., S2K-MCS-...-TOS-GCI, EGOS-GEN-EDDS-...). Provide a version matrix table listing every standard covered by this wiki with the issue we hold, date, status (current/superseded/draft) and link to its library page and topic page. Explain PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A, 2003) vs PUS-C (ECSS-E-ST-70-41C, 2016) vs the Rev.1 DIR1 draft (Dec 2024).

pages.title: Downlink: from on-board parameter to operator display
pages.brief: Step-by-step narrative of the telemetry path with a layer diagram: sampling an on-board parameter, PUS housekeeping/event report generation (ST[03], ST[05]), PUS TM secondary header and time stamp, Space Packet primary header (APID, sequence count), packetisation into TM/AOS transfer frames (virtual channels, master channel, OCF/CLCW, FECF), channel coding and ASM, modulation (one paragraph only), ground station reception and frame sync, SLE return services to the control centre, NCTRS/NIS packet delivery, SCOS-2000 packet identification by APID/type/subtype/PI1/PI2 (MIB PID/PIC tables), parameter extraction (PLF/VPD), calibration (CAF/TXF/MCF/LGF), limit checking (OCF/OCP), archiving and display, and dissemination via EDDS. Each stage links to the detailed page.

pages.title: Uplink: from operator command to on-board execution
pages.brief: Step-by-step narrative of the telecommand path: command definition in the MIB (CCF/CDF/CPC, parameter calibration and range checks PRF/PRV, PAF/PAS, CCA/CCS), command sequences (CSF/CSS/SDF/CSP), stack/manual stack in SCOS-2000, pre-transmission validation (PTV) and interlocks, PUS TC secondary header (ack flags, service type/subtype, source ID), Space Packet primary header, TC transfer frame with segment header/MAP ID, COP-1 (FOP-1 on ground, FARM-1 on board, AD vs BD frames, CLCW feedback in TM OCF), CLTU encoding (BCH, start sequence, tail sequence), physical layer operations procedure (PLOP), SLE FCLTU service from control centre to ground station, and closing the loop with PUS ST[01] request verification reports and MIB command verification (CVS/CVE/CVP). Link to every detailed page.

pages.title: Worked example: decoding a real Solar Orbiter telemetry packet
pages.brief: Using the real Solar Orbiter MIB (SQLite at /home/feiteira/JLF/ESA-OPEN-DOCS/mib-db/solo-2025-09-16.sqlite, tables pid, pic, tpcf, plf, pcf, cur, caf, cap, txf, txp, ocf, ocp, vpd), pick ONE representative fixed-layout housekeeping packet (PUS type 3 subtype 25) with a manageable number of parameters and walk through: how SCOS-2000 identifies it (APID, type, subtype, PI1/PI2 via PIC), its SPID and description, the PLF layout (byte/bit offsets for each parameter, lengths from PTC/PFC), then for 3-5 of its parameters: PCF row, PTC/PFC meaning, calibration curve (numeric or textual) with actual calibration points, limits. Build a bitfield diagram of the packet data field start. Construct an illustrative (clearly labelled synthetic, NOT real downlinked) byte string and decode it step by step, including the Space Packet primary header and PUS-C TM secondary header (check which PUS version and time format Solar Orbiter uses from the MIB/DDID if possible; if not determinable, say so). Provide explorer deep links for the packet and each parameter. Cite the ICD for each table/field meaning and say exactly which MIB release the data comes from.

pages.title: Worked example: building a real Solar Orbiter telecommand
pages.brief: Using the real Solar Orbiter MIB (SQLite /home/feiteira/JLF/ESA-OPEN-DOCS/mib-db/solo-2025-09-16.sqlite, tables ccf, cdf, cpc, prf, prv, paf, pas, cca, ccs, tcp, pcdf, pcpc, cvs, cve, cvp) pick ONE representative, harmless-looking command with 1-3 parameters (for example a housekeeping-report enable or a parameter report request; avoid anything that looks like a safety-critical or irreversible command) and walk through: the CCF row (type/subtype, APID, critical flag, etc.), CDF elements with bit offsets/lengths and fixed vs editable values, CPC parameter definitions, any range checks and calibrations, verification stages (CVS/CVE/CVP) applied to it, packet header definition (TCP/PCPC/PCDF), then assemble the PUS TC secondary header and Space Packet header, the TC transfer frame and CLTU around it (use illustrative values for SCID/VCID/sequence numbers and say so explicitly). Provide explorer deep links for the command. Cite the ICD and the standards for each step.

pages.title: CCSDS: overview of the protocol stack
pages.brief: Introduce CCSDS and its layered architecture per the Overview of Space Communications Protocols (130.0-G-4) and the Space Data Link Protocols summary (130.2-G-3): physical, synchronization and channel coding sublayer, data link protocol sublayer (TM, TC, AOS, Proximity-1, USLP), network (Space Packet, Encapsulation, IP over CCSDS), transport/application (CFDP etc.), cross support (SLE). Explain transfer frames vs packets, virtual channels, master channels, spacecraft identifiers (SCID), managed parameters. Provide a big layer table mapping each layer to the pages in this wiki and the documents in the library.

pages.title: Space Packet Protocol (CCSDS 133.0-B-2)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: purpose and services (packet service, octet string service), the Space Packet structure with a bitfield diagram of the 6-octet primary header (version 000, type, secondary header flag, APID 11 bits incl. idle APID 2047, sequence flags, sequence count or name, data length = octets-1), the packet data field and optional secondary header, maximum length, packet sequence count rules, APID qualifiers, managed parameters, protocol procedures at sending/receiving ends, and how PUS (ECSS-E-ST-70-41C) layers its secondary headers on top. Mention changes between editions if the document's history mentions them.

pages.title: Encapsulation Packet Protocol (CCSDS 133.1-B-3)
pages.brief: Encapsulation packets and the Encapsulation service: header structure (packet version 111, protocol ID, length of length, user defined field, protocol ID extension, CCSDS-defined field, packet length) with bitfield diagram(s) for the variants, idle encapsulation packets, use for carrying IP and other protocol data units over CCSDS links, relation to the IP over CCSDS and to the Space Packet. Explain where an ESA ground segment engineer may meet it.

pages.title: TM Space Data Link Protocol (CCSDS 132.0-B-3)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: TM transfer frame structure with bitfield diagram of the primary header (version, SCID, VCID, OCF flag, MC frame count, VC frame count, frame data field status incl. secondary header flag, sync flag, packet order flag, segment length ID, first header pointer incl. special values 0x7FF/0x7FE), optional secondary header, data field, operational control field (CLCW from COP-1), frame error control field (CRC-16 polynomial), services (VCP, VCA, VC_FSH, VC_OCF, VCF, MCF...), virtual channel multiplexing, idle data, managed parameters, SDLS option. Explain how packets span frames using the first header pointer with a worked illustration.

pages.title: TM synchronization and channel coding (CCSDS 131.0-B-5)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the synchronization and channel coding sublayer for TM/AOS/USLP: attached sync marker (ASM 0x1ACFFC1D and others), CADU, pseudo-randomization (polynomial, when required), Reed-Solomon (255,223) with interleaving depths and virtual fill, convolutional coding (rate 1/2, K=7, punctured rates), concatenated coding, turbo codes, LDPC codes, frame validation, transfer frame lengths allowed with each code, and the rationale from the Green Book 130.1-G-3 (coding gain, performance). Use tables. Keep maths readable (MathJax allowed).

pages.title: TC Space Data Link Protocol (CCSDS 232.0-B-4)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: TC transfer frame structure with bitfield diagram of the 5-octet primary header (version, bypass flag, control command flag, reserved, SCID, VCID, frame length, frame sequence number), frame data field, optional segment header (sequence flags, MAP ID) and the MAP/segmentation sublayer, frame error control field, AD/BD/BC frame types, services (MAP packet, VC packet, VC frame, MC frame...), managed parameters, relation to COP-1 and to SDLS. Include the meaning of control commands (Unlock, Set V(R)).

pages.title: COP-1: FOP-1, FARM-1 and the CLCW (CCSDS 232.1-B-2)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the Communications Operation Procedure-1: purpose (go-back-n ARQ for TC), FOP-1 (sending end) states, variables V(S), NN(R), sliding window, timers, Initiate AD service modes, FARM-1 (receiving end) states (Open, Wait, Lockout), variables V(R), window width, positive/negative windows, the CLCW structure with bitfield diagram (control word type, version, status, COP in effect, VCID, flags: no RF available, no bit lock, lockout, wait, retransmit, FARM-B counter, report value), how the CLCW is returned in the TM OCF, and common operational situations (lockout recovery with Unlock, Set V(R)). Use state tables and a mermaid state diagram.

pages.title: TC synchronization and channel coding: the CLTU (CCSDS 231.0-B-4)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the CLTU structure (start sequence 0xEB90, BCH(63,56) codeblocks with filler and parity, tail sequence), the modified BCH code details, optional pseudo-randomization, LDPC options for TC, the Physical Layer Operations Procedures PLOP-1 and PLOP-2 (carrier modulation modes, acquisition and idle sequences), error-correcting vs error-detecting decoding modes, and rationale from the Green Book 230.1-G-3. Include a bitfield/structure diagram of a CLTU.

pages.title: AOS Space Data Link Protocol (CCSDS 732.0-B-4)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: AOS transfer frame (primary header with version 01, SCID, VCID, VC frame count, signalling field incl. replay flag and VC frame count usage, optional frame header error control), insert zone, M_PDU (first header pointer) and B_PDU (bitstream data pointer) data field types, OCF, FECF, services (packet, bitstream, VCA, insert...), comparison with TM frames and when missions choose AOS. Bitfield diagrams for header and M_PDU header.

pages.title: Unified Space Data Link Protocol (CCSDS 732.1-B-3)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: USLP transfer frame primary header (version 1100, SCID 16 bits, source/destination flag, VCID, MAP ID, end of frame primary header flag, frame length, bypass/sequence control flag, protocol control command flag, OCF flag, VC frame count length and count), truncated frames, transfer frame data field header (construction rules, protocol ID, first header/last valid octet pointer), insert zone, OCF, FECF, services, how USLP unifies TM/TC/AOS, and its use with SDLS. Bitfield diagrams.

pages.title: Space Data Link Security (CCSDS 355.0-B-2)
pages.brief: Comprehensive but careful: the SDLS protocol's purpose (authentication, encryption, authenticated encryption at the data link layer), security header (SPI, IV, sequence number, pad length) and trailer (MAC), security associations and their management, how it plugs into TM/TC/AOS/USLP frames, anti-replay, and the separation from key management. Describe the standard, do not give attack guidance.

pages.title: Time code formats (CCSDS 301.0-B-4)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: CCSDS Unsegmented time Code (CUC) with P-field and T-field, coarse/fine octets, epochs (1958 TAI, agency-defined); CCSDS Day Segmented (CDS) code; Calendar Segmented (CCS) code; ASCII calendar codes A and B; leap seconds handling; with bitfield diagrams for P-fields. Then explain how PUS packet time stamps (ECSS-E-ST-70-41C time field, PTC 9/10 absolute/relative time) and SCOS-2000 time correlation (OBT to UTC, TN-1030) use these codes.

pages.title: CCSDS File Delivery Protocol (CCSDS 727.0-B-5)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: CFDP entities, transactions, unacknowledged and acknowledged modes, PDU types (file directive PDUs: EOF, Finished, ACK, Metadata, NAK, Prompt, Keep Alive; file data PDU), fixed PDU header bitfield diagram, segmentation, checksums, user operations, store-and-forward overlay, relation to PUS ST[23] file management and ST[13] large packet transfer for missions that do not use CFDP.

pages.title: XTCE: XML Telemetric and Command Exchange (CCSDS 660)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: what XTCE is (OMG standard adopted by CCSDS 660.0-B-2), its main elements (SpaceSystem, TelemetryMetaData, ParameterTypeSet, ParameterSet, ContainerSet, CommandMetaData, MetaCommandSet, algorithms) per the Green Book 660.1-G-2, and a careful concept mapping to the SCOS-2000 MIB tables (PCF<->Parameter/ParameterType, PID/PLF<->SequenceContainer, CAF/TXF<->calibrators, CCF/CDF/CPC<->MetaCommand/arguments, OCF/OCP<->alarms). Flag mapping judgements as this wiki's analysis, not a standard.

pages.title: Space Link Extension (SLE): concept and architecture
pages.brief: Comprehensive: why SLE exists (cross support between agencies' ground stations and control centres), the cross support concept (910.3-G-3): space link services vs SLE services, return vs forward services, service production vs provision, online/offline delivery, service instances, BIND/START/STOP/UNBIND operations, service management; list of SLE transfer services (RAF, RCF, ROCF, FCLTU, FSP...) and how ESA's ground segment uses them (with NCTRS/NIS and the ESA SLE API). Link to each service page.

pages.title: SLE return services: RAF, RCF and ROCF
pages.brief: Comprehensive: Return All Frames (911.1-B-5), Return Channel Frames (911.2-B-4), Return Operational Control Fields (911.5-B-4): purpose, service parameters, delivery modes (timely online, complete online, offline), operations (RAF-START with frame quality filter, TRANSFER-DATA, SYNC-NOTIFY, GET-PARAMETER, SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT), state machines, production status, how CLCWs reach the control centre via ROCF.

pages.title: SLE forward service: FCLTU
pages.brief: Comprehensive: Forward CLTU service (912.1-B-5): purpose, CLTU-TRANSFER-DATA with earliest/latest radiation time and delay, CLTU-ASYNC-NOTIFY, THROW-EVENT, production status and uplink status, buffer management, state machine, parameters, and how this connects to the CLTU encoding page and to SCOS-2000/NIS 'throw events'.

pages.title: SLE over TCP/IP (ISP1) and the SLE API
pages.brief: Comprehensive: Internet SLE Protocol One (913.1-B-2): TML (transport mapping layer) messages over TCP, heartbeat, context message, authentication (credentials), PDU encoding (ASN.1 BER), and the SLE API (914.0-M-2): API architecture, components (API proxy, service element, ...), interfaces, and how implementations (e.g. ESA's SLE API) use it.

pages.title: ECSS: the European space standards system
pages.brief: Explain ECSS (European Cooperation for Space Standardization), branches (E engineering, Q, M, U), document types (ST standards, HB handbooks, AS adoption notices of CCSDS, TM technical memoranda, DIR drafts), the E-50 communications and E-70 ground systems & operations families and their members relevant here (E-ST-50C, E-ST-50-03C (cancelled, superseded by adoption notices E-AS-50-22C/23C), E-AS-50-25C Rev.1 (TC SDLP), E-AS-50-26C (COP-1), E-HB-50A, E-ST-70-11C, E-ST-70-31C, E-ST-70-41C). Table with links.

pages.title: ECSS-E-ST-50C communications and the CCSDS adoption notices
pages.brief: Comprehensive: scope of ECSS-E-ST-50C Rev.1 (space communications requirements, link layers, RF), its structure, what the adoption notices change compared to the CCSDS books (E-AS-50-25C Rev.1 for TC SDLP 232.0-B-4, E-AS-50-26C for COP-1 232.1-B-2), the historical ECSS-E-ST-50-03C TM transfer frame standard and its cancellation, and the guidance in ECSS-E-HB-50A (communications guidelines handbook) on link design choices.

pages.title: ECSS-E-ST-70-31C: monitoring and control data definition
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the space system model (system elements, activities, reporting data, events), parameter definitions, calibration, monitoring checks, activities (telecommands, procedures), the data definition life cycle, and an explicit comparison with how the SCOS-2000 MIB realises those concepts (PCF/OCF/CCF etc.).

pages.title: ECSS-E-ST-70-11C: space segment operability
pages.brief: Comprehensive: what operability requirements cover (observability, commandability, autonomy, FDIR, on-board time, data handling, PUS usage), the Rev.1 (Oct 2025) relationship to ECSS-E-ST-70-41 for packet utilisation, and how operability requirements show up in the MIB and PUS services.

pages.title: PUS: the Packet Utilization Standard
pages.brief: Comprehensive introduction to ECSS-E-ST-70-41C (15 April 2016): purpose, history (ECSS-E-70-41A 2003; ECSS-E-70-41B never issued; Rev.1 DIR1 Dec 2024 draft), the PUS architecture (application processes, services, subservices, capability sets, requests vs reports, message type notation TC[x,y]/TM[x,y], service type identifiers ST[xx]), tailoring by missions, and a table of all standard services with links to each service page in this wiki. Use the Valera status presentations for context on the 2016 revision.

pages.title: PUS packet structures: TC and TM headers
pages.brief: Comprehensive: PUS-C telecommand packet (primary header + TC secondary header: PUS version number, acknowledgement flags, service type, subtype, source ID, spare) and telemetry packet (TM secondary header: PUS version, spacecraft time reference status, service type, subtype, message type counter, destination ID, time, spare), packet error control (CRC-16 CCITT, ISO checksum), with bitfield diagrams; then the PUS-A (2003) equivalents (CCSDS secondary header flag, PUS version 1, ack bits, packet subcounter, etc.) side by side. Explain how SCOS-2000 MIB PID_DFHSIZE and TCP/PCDF definitions describe these headers.

pages.title: PUS parameter types (PTC/PFC)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the PUS parameter type code / parameter format code system from ECSS-E-ST-70-41C clause 7 (Boolean PTC 1, enumerated PTC 2, unsigned PTC 3, signed PTC 4, real PTC 5, bit-string PTC 6, octet-string PTC 7, character-string PTC 8, absolute time PTC 9, relative time PTC 10, deduced PTC 11, packet PTC 12 ...) with a full table of PFC values and bit lengths, compared with PUS-A definitions, and how the SCOS-2000 MIB uses PTC/PFC in PCF/CPC (including any SCOS-specific restrictions or extensions such as PTC 13 or PFC values for time listed in the ICD).

pages.title: PUS-A vs PUS-C (and the 2024 Rev.1 draft)
pages.brief: Comprehensive comparison: service list changes (numbering, new services such as ST[20], ST[21], ST[22], ST[23], removed/merged ones), header changes, capability set concept, report naming, time formats, and what the Rev.1 DIR1 (Dec 2024) proposes to change. Tables with clause references in each document.

pages.title: ST[01] Request verification
pages.brief: Full service description from ECSS-E-ST-70-41C: purpose, subservices, every message type TM[1,1]..TM[1,10] with name and data field layout (request ID, failure notice codes), acceptance/start/progress/completion verification, ack flags in TC header, capability sets, PUS-A differences, and how SCOS-2000 MIB command verification (CVS/CVE/CVP) and Solar Orbiter's MIB use it (query the SQLite DB /home/feiteira/JLF/ESA-OPEN-DOCS/mib-db/solo-2025-09-16.sqlite: pid where PID_TYPE=1, ccf where CCF_TYPE=1).

pages.title: ST[02] Device access
pages.brief: Full service description from ECSS-E-ST-70-41C: on/off device commands, register load/dump, physical/logical device access, CPDU commands, every message type with data field structure, capability sets, PUS-A differences; Solar Orbiter MIB usage (packets/commands with type 2).

pages.title: ST[03] Housekeeping
pages.brief: Full service description from ECSS-E-ST-70-41C: housekeeping and diagnostic parameter report structures, create/delete/enable/disable/modify/report definitions, collection intervals, super-commutated parameters, periodic generation, every message type TC[3,x]/TM[3,x] with data fields, capability sets; PUS-A differences (service 3 subtypes); how SCOS-2000 decodes HK packets via PID/PLF/VPD and SID as PI1; Solar Orbiter MIB statistics (count of TM[3,25]/[3,26] packets, how SIDs appear in PIC/PID_PI1_VAL).

pages.title: ST[04] Parameter statistics reporting
pages.brief: Full service description from ECSS-E-ST-70-41C with all message types, data fields, capability sets, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter MIB usage if any.

pages.title: ST[05] Event reporting
pages.brief: Full service description: event report severities (informative, low, medium, high), event definitions, enable/disable, report list of disabled events, all message types and data fields, capability sets, PUS-A differences; SCOS-2000 event packets (PID_EVENT, PID_EVID) and Solar Orbiter MIB usage (count of type 5 packets, examples of event descriptions).

pages.title: ST[06] Memory management
pages.brief: Full service description: raw and object memory access, load, dump, check (checksum), memory IDs, all message types and data fields, capability sets, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter MIB usage.

pages.title: ST[08] Function management
pages.brief: Full service description: perform function TC[8,1], function IDs and arguments, capability sets, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[09] Time management
pages.brief: Full service description: time reports (CUC/CDS time reports TM[9,2]/TM[9,3]), time report generation rate, spacecraft time reference status, all message types and data fields, PUS-A differences; link to CCSDS time codes and SCOS-2000 time correlation (TN-1030).

pages.title: ST[11] Time-based scheduling
pages.brief: Full service description: the time-based schedule, sub-schedules, groups, insert/delete/time-shift activities, enable/disable, summary and detail reports, all message types and data fields, capability sets, PUS-A differences (service 11 in PUS-A), Solar Orbiter usage (ccf with type 11) and how SCOS-2000 handles time-tagged commands (CCF/CDF time tag fields if present).

pages.title: ST[12] On-board monitoring
pages.brief: Full service description: parameter monitoring definitions (limit, expected value, delta checks), check transitions, functional monitoring, all message types and data fields, capability sets, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[13] Large packet transfer
pages.brief: Full service description: up/down link large message transfer by parts, first/intermediate/last part, abort, all message types and data fields, PUS-A differences, and Solar Orbiter's custom s13a/s13p/s13t MIB tables (inspect them in the SQLite DB and explain what they appear to contain, flagged as inference).

pages.title: ST[14] Real-time forwarding control
pages.brief: Full service description: application process forward-control configuration, housekeeping/event report forwarding control, all message types and data fields, PUS-A differences (packet forwarding control), Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[15] On-board storage and retrieval
pages.brief: Full service description: packet stores (circular/bounded), storage control, retrieval by time window or by-packet, open/closed retrieval, downlink, all message types and data fields, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter usage and relation to playback telemetry (VC usage).

pages.title: ST[17] Test
pages.brief: Full service description: are-you-alive connection test, on-board connection test, all message types, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[18] On-board operations procedure
pages.brief: Full service description: OBCP load/unload/activate/stop/suspend/resume, parameters, all message types and data fields, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[19] Event-action
pages.brief: Full service description: event-action definitions, enable/disable, reports, all message types and data fields, PUS-A differences, Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[20] On-board parameter management
pages.brief: Full service description: report/set parameter values, parameter definition management, all message types and data fields, Solar Orbiter usage; mention Solar Orbiter's ASW_sw_para MIB table and its possible relation (inspect, flag as inference).

pages.title: ST[21] Request sequencing
pages.brief: Full service description: on-board request sequences, load/unload/activate/abort, all message types and data fields, Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: ST[22] Position-based scheduling
pages.brief: Full service description: orbit-position-based schedule, all message types and data fields, Solar Orbiter usage (likely none; check).

pages.title: ST[23] File management
pages.brief: Full service description: file systems, create/delete/report attributes, lock/unlock, find, copy/move, directory summary, all message types and data fields, relation to CFDP; Solar Orbiter usage.

pages.title: PUS message type catalogue
pages.brief: A complete, sortable catalogue (one big table) of every standard PUS-C message type TC[x,y]/TM[x,y] in ECSS-E-ST-70-41C with its name, request/report, and link to the service page; plus a second table showing, for the Solar Orbiter MIB (SQLite /home/feiteira/JLF/ESA-OPEN-DOCS/mib-db/solo-2025-09-16.sqlite), the count of TM packet definitions (pid) and TC definitions (ccf) per (type, subtype), marking mission-specific (non-standard) types. Clearly state the MIB release.

pages.title: SCOS-2000: ESA's mission control system
pages.brief: Comprehensive overview & history: SCOS-I, SCOS-II (OL language), SCOS-2000 origins (late 1990s), releases (R2.x used for Herschel/Planck EGSE, R3, R4, R5 in 2006 with re-engineered TM chain, R6...), missions using it, licensing (ESA convention, MICONYS under ESA Software Community License), community (users workshop), SPEC certification (ESA Bulletin 115), cost-reduction context (Bulletin 130 'Happy families'), and the evolution toward EGS-CC. Timeline (mermaid timeline or table).

pages.title: SCOS-2000 architecture
pages.brief: Comprehensive: client-server architecture, main applications (task launcher, TM desktop, alphanumeric/graphic/scrolling displays, out-of-limits display, event logger, manual stack, command history, packet displays), TM chain (packetiser, parameter processing, OOL checking), TC chain (command sources, release, verification), archives (history files, file archive), OL synthetic parameters, events & actions, external interfaces (EXIF / CORBA, TOPE), configuration (MISCconfig), MIB import, multi-domain/multi-spacecraft; use the user guide for the impatient, EMCS SUM, TN-1030, MIB ICD 7.0 references and the Planck LFI paper.

pages.title: SCOS-2000 as EGSE and central checkout
pages.brief: Comprehensive: 'EGSE based on SCOS 2000' (EMCS SUM issue 4.0, 2004): EMCS kernel, Space System Model, TOPE test procedure language, SCOEs, EGSE router, gateway ICD, TCL scripts; the Herschel/Planck EGSE (common EGSE documents, integration plan, TEI TM/TC packet ICD, CCS IEGSE TC interface, EGSE general requirements spec H-P-1-ASPI-SP-0045), commercial CCS (Terma CCS5/TSC, right-sizing test tools), the SRDB translator (S2K to ECHO), and the TOPE to EGS-CC migration paper.

pages.title: EDDS: EGOS Data Dissemination System
pages.brief: Comprehensive: EDDS purpose, history (successor of GDDS, TDRS, WebRM, MUST per the SRS), architecture from the SDD (web portal, standalone client, ActiveMQ broker, XFDU library, SFT for firewall crossing, data providers PARC/DARC/FARC), services from the EUICD (authentication, batch requests, stream requests, user management), request types and output formats, the document set with versions (EUICD v13/15/24, SDD 15/25, SUM 14/22, CIG 14/25, EUG 12, SRN 14, GLO 7), noting that some file names do not match the version printed inside (e.g. file 'EUICD.v25' is Version 24.0; 'CIG.v24' and 'SDD.v24' are Version 25.0).

pages.title: EDDS request and data formats
pages.brief: Comprehensive: XML request structures for batch and stream requests (packet TM, TC, events, parameters, files), response packaging (XFDU), binary packet layouts (EDDS TM/TC packet structures, GDDS binary format with its header fields), example requests/responses (paraphrased, short), and the Solar Orbiter DDID specifics (which data types, which archive answers, RAPID file naming). Bitfield diagrams for binary record headers.

pages.title: TDRS: Telemetry Data Retrieval Service
pages.brief: Comprehensive: TDRS role (retrieval of telemetry from SCOS-2000 history files for external users), architecture (web server, PCGI, PRQM via CORBA, PSRV via TCP/IP), retrieval request file (.req) with fast/fast-with-engineering/complete retrievals, filters, time windows, result formats (MVDA, spreadsheet .fst/.fen/.cmp, column-organised .col), user log; WebRM; how TDRS requirements fed EDDS. Plus the Venus Express ground segment description.

pages.title: GDDS and mission data delivery interface documents
pages.brief: Comprehensive: GDDS (Generic Data Disposition System) as described by the Rosetta/Mars Express/Venus Express DDID (RO-ESC-IF-5003 issues B5, C2, appendix I C3 XML schemas incl. GDDSCommon.xsd), the Mars Express data handling chapter (ESA SP-1291), request/delivery types, the GDDS binary format, and how the Solar Orbiter DDID (SOL-ESC-IF-05011) carries these conventions into EDDS. Tables of data types per mission.

pages.title: Mission archives: PARC, DARC and FARC
pages.brief: What is publicly documented about the packet archive (PARC), parameter archive (DARC; the EDDS glossary also expands it 'Data Archive') and file archive (FARC): which data each holds, how EDDS queries them (SDD data providers, Solar Orbiter DDID sections), RAPID file naming, MIB-related content in FARC (TC sequences and TM display definitions as XML since ICD issue 6.4), and the documents that exist but are not public (DARC ICD/SDD, Analysis of Web Services and PARC). Be explicit about gaps.

pages.title: NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface
pages.brief: Comprehensive with available sources: NCTRS (Network Control and TM/TC Router System) and its successor NIS (Network Interface System) as gateway between ESTRACK stations and mission control systems, packet/frame routing, the IFMS (Intermediate Frequency and Modem System) to OCC FTP interface (IFMS-OCC ICD issue 11.4.0) including file types for ranging/Doppler/meteo, the MCS-FDS ICD use of NIS for tracking data, the DLR SLE switchboard and NCTRS-protocol use in GECCOS (SpaceOps 2021, 4S 2024), and the NIS throw events. Be explicit about what is not public (NCTRS/NIS ICD volumes).

pages.title: Time correlation in SCOS-2000
pages.brief: Comprehensive from EGOS-MCS-S2K-TN-1030 v1.0 (2018): on-board time (OBT) vs UTC, time correlation packets and coefficients, the TCO configuration, the OBT-to-UTC conversion API, the time correlation packetiser, ground station delays, accuracy, and links to CCSDS CUC and PUS ST[09].

pages.title: Ancillary systems, MICONYS and the move to EGS-CC
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the ESOC ground segment software infrastructure picture (GSAW 2005), MICONYS (SCOS-2000 and ancillary applications: EDDS, ARES, MUST, MOIS, ProToS, MATIS, DABYS, FOPPER, OPEN-M as named in sources), ARES data analytics (GSAW 2020), EGS-CC (European Ground Systems Common Core) and ESOC's adoption (Pecchioli paper, SpaceOps 2025 Reggestad & Widegard, EGOS-CC SESP 2019, TOPE integration with EGS-CC), mission products delivery standard (SpaceOps 2025 #309), payload commanding request framework (SpaceOps 2025 #141). Mermaid timeline.

pages.title: Herschel/Planck: SCOS-2000 in a science mission ground segment
pages.brief: Comprehensive case study: the 2000 decision to base FIRST/Planck EGSE and MCS on SCOS-2000 (April 2000 ESOC meeting minutes, presentations, evaluation, licence terms), HCSS (Herschel Common Science System) interfaces: TC history ingestion, TC history/out-of-limits ingestion user guide, MIB clarification and tailoring note, SPIRE database management and configuration control, the HPSDB/MIB processing technical note (Alcatel H-P-1-ASP-TN-1060), operations interface requirements (SCI-PT-RS-07360), NLR ACMS database experience, and the Herschel MIB in the archive (access currently returns HTTP 403 for the zip files).

pages.title: The MIB: Mission Information Base
pages.brief: Comprehensive introduction: what the MIB is (the SCOS-2000 run-time database populated from ASCII tables defined by the Database Import ICD EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001), file format (one .dat file per table, tab-separated, one record per line, field order fixed, mandatory/optional fields, character set), the import process and consistency checks, the ICD scope (generic part only; mission-specific extensions allowed), how missions generate MIBs (from spacecraft/instrument databases via tools like DBM, SRDB), the role of MIB versions (VDF), and a map of the table families (monitoring, displays, commanding, verification, sequences, parameter sets) with links to every table page under mib/tables/. Include a short tour of the real Solar Orbiter MIB (row counts per table from the SQLite DB).

pages.title: MIB data model: how the tables relate
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the table relationship overview from the ICD (primary keys and foreign keys between tables), presented as mermaid erDiagram(s) split into monitoring, commanding, verification/sequences, displays; plus prose walking the main join paths (packet -> PID -> PLF -> PCF -> CUR -> CAF/TXF/MCF/LGF; parameter -> OCF/OCP; command -> CCF -> CDF -> CPC -> PRF/PAF/CCA; command -> CVS via CVP; sequence -> CSF -> CSS -> SDF/CSP). Verify key names against the ICD and against the real data (SQLite).

pages.title: MIB parameter types: PTC/PFC in SCOS-2000
pages.brief: Comprehensive: the ICD's tables of allowed PTC/PFC combinations for monitoring (PCF) and commanding (CPC) parameters, bit widths, SCOS-specific types (e.g. PTC 11 deduced, PTC 13 SCOS-2000 parameter types if listed), endianness (PCF_ENDIAN if present), how these relate to PUS (link to the PUS parameter types page), and a frequency table of PTC/PFC combinations actually used in the Solar Orbiter MIB (SQLite).

pages.title: History of the Database Import ICD (issues 5.1 to 7.2)
pages.brief: Comprehensive: reconstruct the change history from the change logs in issues 5.1 (2001), 6.7 Draft A (2009), 6.9 (2010), 7.0 (2017) and what is known about 7.2 (2019, via pyscos2000): tables added/removed (e.g. TC sequences and TM displays moved to XML in FARC from issue 6.4), field additions, SCOS-2000 release mapping (R2.3, R3, R4.5, R5.x, R6...). Table of issues with dates, releases and key changes, each cited.

pages.title: Monitoring in the MIB: parameters and packets
pages.brief: Comprehensive: monitoring parameters (PCF fields: name, description, PID, unit, PTC/PFC, width, validity parameter and value, related parameter, category, nature (raw/dynamic OL/synthetic/hard-coded/saved synthetic/constant), calibration curve set, interpolation, use calibrated, decimals, default value, subsystem, OBT ID, DARC flag, endianness), packet identification (PID/PIC/TPCF: APID, type, subtype, PI1/PI2 position and width, SPID, TPSD, DFH size, time/event flags), fixed packet layout (PLF: offsets in bytes/bits, occurrence count, time offset for super-commutated samples), variable packets (VPD: repetition groups, choice, display formats), groups (GRP/GRPA/GRPK). Use real Solar Orbiter examples with explorer deep links.

pages.title: Calibration in the MIB
pages.brief: Comprehensive: numerical calibration curves (CAF/CAP: engineering format, raw format, radix, interpolation/extrapolation), textual calibrations (TXF/TXP: from/to raw ranges to text), polynomial (MCF: A0..A4), logarithmic (LGF), calibration selection by CUR (conditional curves based on another parameter's value), PCF_CURTX and PCF_INTER, and command-side calibrations (CCA/CCS numeric, PAF/PAS textual de-calibration) with links. Real Solar Orbiter examples with numbers (query SQLite) and explorer deep links.

pages.title: Monitoring checks: limits and out-of-limits
pages.brief: Comprehensive: OCF (number of checks, interpretation, coded/uncoded) and OCP (limit types: soft/hard limits, delta, event, status consistency, low/high values, RLCHK/VALPAR applicability conditions), status consistency checking, how SCOS-2000 flags OOL and feeds the OOL display and event logger, and examples from Solar Orbiter MIB (SQLite) with explorer deep links. Relate to PUS ST[12] on-board monitoring (ground vs on-board checks).

pages.title: Commanding in the MIB: commands and their parameters
pages.brief: Comprehensive: CCF (command name, description, CNAME, type/subtype, APID, NPARS, PLAN/EXEC flags, ILSCOPE/ILSTAGE interlocks, subsystem, hazardous/critical flag, MAPID, DEFSET, RAPID, ACK, SUBSCHEDID, ...), DST (destination), CDF (command element definition: element type fixed/editable/spare, length, bit offset, group size, default value), CPC (command parameter: PTC/PFC, display format, radix, unit, category, PRF/CCA/PAF references, inter, default value...), PRF/PRV range checks, PAF/PAS textual de-calibration, CCA/CCS numeric de-calibration, TCP/PCPC/PCDF packet header definitions, PTV pre-transmission validation. Real Solar Orbiter examples with explorer deep links.

pages.title: Command verification in the MIB
pages.brief: Comprehensive: CVS (verification stage: type acceptance/start/progress/completion, source (R reports / V parameters), time window start/span, uncertainty), CVE (verification expressions on parameters: comparison values, tolerance), CVP (command-to-verification-profile mapping), how SCOS-2000 combines them with PUS ST[01] reports; Solar Orbiter examples (query SQLite cvs/cve/cvp — note their column names are not in our auto schema: derive them from the ICD) with explorer deep links.

pages.title: Command sequences and parameter sets
pages.brief: Comprehensive: CSF (sequence header: name, description, number of formal parameters, IFTT, DFTT, subsystem, ...), CSS (sequence elements: commands/sub-sequences/textual comments, relative release times, time tags), SDF (element parameter values), CSP (sequence formal parameters); parameter sets PST/PSV/CPS/PVS/PSM; the move of sequences to XML in the FARC for SCOS-2000 R5+ (ICD 6.4+). Solar Orbiter examples with explorer deep links.

pages.title: Display definitions in the MIB
pages.brief: Comprehensive: alphanumeric displays (DPF/DPC), graphical displays (GPF/GPC), scrolling displays (SPF/SPC), printout definitions (PPF/PPC), groups (GRP/GRPA/GRPK), what each field controls, the XML-in-FARC change, and what Solar Orbiter's MIB contains (row counts, examples).

pages.title: Synthetic parameters and the OL language
pages.brief: Comprehensive: PCF_NATUR values for synthetic/dynamic/hard-coded/saved synthetic parameters, the Operations Language (OL) syntax used in synthetic parameter definition files (from the ICD and the SCOS-II OL paper), examples from the real Solar Orbiter MIB synthetic folder (SQLite table 'synthetic' with NAME and SOURCE), explaining 2-3 real expressions line by line (e.g. a quaternion-to-angle conversion), and statistics (how many, which subsystems).

pages.title: Mission tailoring of the MIB
pages.brief: Comprehensive: how projects tailor/constrain the generic ICD: the HCSS MIB Clarification and Tailoring Note (HSC/DOC/0300 issue 1.5), SPIRE MIB naming convention, Alcatel Herschel/Planck faxes imposing naming limits and constraints (e.g. PID_SPID = PID_TPSD, PCF_WIDTH not Null; the March 2003 fax is a scan: its content is summarised from a manual reading), HPSDB MIB processing TN, SPIRE DB management/configuration control, and Solar Orbiter's non-ICD tables (ASW_sw_para, pcf_glob_det, dup, s13a/s13p/s13t: inspect columns and values in SQLite and describe them, flagged as inference).

pages.title: MIB tooling and open-source libraries
pages.brief: Comprehensive: Terma Data Base Manager (DBM), the HIFI MIB editor requirements and evaluation of ESOC's Integral MS-Access DB editing subsystem, SRDB translator (S2K to ECHO), pyscos2000 (MIT, IRF, schemas from ICD 7.2), scospus (MIT, IRF, PUS packet interpretation using a MIB), SCOSpy (GPL-3.0, INAF, SCOS-2000 header decoding for BepiColombo/JUICE), mib-generator (MIT, builds MIBs from C headers), edds_process (Paris Observatory, EDDS XML), and this site's own build scripts. Table with licences, versions and links. Verify the facts you state about pypi packages via the PyPI JSON API (https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json) if you can.

pages.title: Solar Orbiter
pages.brief: Mission data systems overview from available documents: MOC, EDDS-based data delivery per the DDID, the EFECS ICD (SOL-SGS-ICD-0006) and SOL-SGS-TN-0007, the Airbus/Astrium TN SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079 (identify what it is), the MIB releases hosted by the SWA/PAS team at IRAP (111 releases 2020-2025), and links to the MIB page, PUS usage page, SWA page and the explorer.

pages.title: The Solar Orbiter MIB
pages.brief: Data-driven analysis of the real MIB (SQLite solo-2025-09-16 and solo-2020-04-16): release naming (MIB__YYYYMMDDMdddPFMS001_SOL where ddd matches day of year; PFMS meaning unknown), row counts per table and growth 2020->2025, subsystem breakdown (PCF_SUBSYS values and parameter-name prefixes with counts), APID catalogue (distinct PID_APID with packet counts, type/subtype distribution), largest packets, calibration counts, synthetic parameter counts, commands per APID/type, and a 2020 vs 2025 diff summary (parameters/packets/commands added/removed). Include explorer deep links for interesting entries. All numbers must come from your own SQL queries (show the queries in a collapsed details block).

pages.title: How Solar Orbiter uses PUS
pages.brief: Data-driven: from pid (TM) and ccf (TC) tables, list which PUS services and subservices the mission uses, how many packet/command definitions each has, mission-specific services/subtypes (outside the ECSS-E-ST-70-41C standard set), event packets, SIDs; link every service to its ECSS page. Note the PUS version (A or C) if it can be determined from the documents/MIB (e.g. TCP/PCDF header definitions, DFH sizes); otherwise say it cannot be determined.

pages.title: Solar Orbiter SWA instrument database
pages.brief: The Solar Wind Analyser (SWA) instrument database in MIB-style tables (SQLite swa-idb.sqlite, from IRAP's ASCII.zip): row counts, APIDs, packets, parameter prefixes, how it relates to the spacecraft MIB (are its parameters present in the full MIB? check by name), and what the SWA_IDB release notes say (if you can't access them, say the notes exist at https://solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu/MIB/ and were not copied).

pages.title: Missions
pages.brief: Index of missions covered by this wiki and what data/documents are available for each: Solar Orbiter (full MIB), Herschel/Planck (HPSDB description, MIB zips not accessible: HTTP 403), Rosetta/Mars Express/Venus Express (DDIDs, GDDS), XMM-Newton/Integral/others (SCOS-2000 users), BepiColombo/JUICE (SCOSpy header IDs). Table of missions with links.

pages.title: Herschel and Planck
pages.brief: The Herschel-Planck Spacecraft Database (HPSDB/MIB), its versions (MOC issues 2-13, 2009-2011), the format references (ICD issue 6.6 and HSC/DOC/0300 1.9), the Planck LFI telemetry handling paper (SCOS-based LFI ground segment, PIPE protocol), the NLR ACMS database experience report, and the instrument EGSE history; link to the Herschel/Planck ground segment page.

pages.title: Rosetta, Mars Express and Venus Express
pages.brief: The shared MCS family and its data delivery (RO/MEX/VEX-ESC-IF-5003 DDID, GDDS), the MCS-FDS ICD (tracking data via NIS into FARC), IFMS radio-science data, the Mars Express data handling chapter (SP-1291), and the Venus Express ground segment paper (VMCS on SCOS-2000, TDRS, VDDS).

pages.title: Other missions and SCOS-2000 users
pages.brief: What the sources say about other SCOS-2000 users and related missions: XMM-Newton (migration from SCOS-I), Integral, Cryosat/GOCE (Earth Explorer MCS kernel), BepiColombo and JUICE (SCOSpy mission/spacecraft IDs; payload request frameworks), Proba (EGSE router), Sentinel/Galileo instrument-level checkout (Terma), and EGS-CC era missions. Only state facts present in the library sources (cite them); if a fact comes from web search during this session, add the URL as a footnote.
